title: A lucky observation of an enigmatic cloud
caption: The nebula IRAS 05437+2502, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A little-known nebula billows out among bright stars and dark dust clouds in this Hubble image, with a bright, sharp-edged boomerang-shaped arc standing out. The nebula is IRAS 05437+2502, in Taurus, the Bull, near the central plane of the Milky Way.

Few detailed studies of it exist, unlike many objects Hubble looks at, so what it really is remains uncertain. On a first look it looks like a small, fairly isolated star-forming region, shaped by ultraviolet light from young stars.

The boomerang arc may tell a more dramatic story. It could have been created by a fast young star ploughing through the cloud of gas and dust. Such a star would have been thrown out of the distant young cluster where it formed, and would be racing through the nebula at 200 000 km/hour or more.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys combined yellow (F606W) and near-infrared (F814W) filters, with about eleven minutes per filter; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and eleven-minute exposures reveal faint gas well beyond naked-eye reach.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/Hubble, R. Sahai and NASA
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The Infrared Astronomical Satellite, IRAS, found this cloud in 1983; it was the first space telescope to map the entire sky in infrared. Hubble took this picture as part of a snapshot survey, filling gaps in its schedule with no guarantee the observation would happen at all.
alt: A billowing nebula among bright stars and dark dust, with a bright sharp-edged boomerang-shaped arc.
